title.narrative: CapaCare Capacity Building in Surgical Care 2024-2028

description.narrative: CapaCare is training medical professionals in the areas where there is a shortage of such personnel. The aim of the surgical training programme is to increase the level of surgical skilled health staff at district hospitals in Sierra Leone. The goal of this programme is to train, each for 2 years, Medical Doctors (MD) and /or nurses and community Health Officers (CHOs) for the country's district hospitals, to be able to handle the most common surgical and obstetrical emergencies that without treatment would lead to disability or death. CapaCare has a focus on increasing the quality of surgical and obstetric provision by offering courses in quality improvement and research methodology to MD candidates. As part of the courses, the students have a mandatory six-month assignment of undertaking a quality improvement assessment. Bi-annual studies of surgical site infection and postoperative mortality are also planned to be part of the mandatory assignments. There is moreover a focus on disseminating the results from the projects through presentations and peer-reviewed publications.
